description: This is a group of 9th grade Korean students.
summary:
We developed a game called "Project: Nasareth". It is a roguelite, RPG inspired space exploration and survival game combining rocket customization, resource management, and mission planning. The story begins with NASA's ambitious spacecraft, Project: Genesis, being destroyed by an asteroid, scattering its modules around the solar system. WIth NASA's resources nearly exhausted, the player is given a basic spacecraft capable of reaching only the Moon and gradually explore farther planets to recover the lost parts.

Throughout the game, players collect resources, earn credits, and design and upgrade their rockets, eventually collecting the original modules of Project: Genesis. 

Our project addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by transforming complex engineering concepts, resource management, and mission-planning trade-offs into an engaging game. We combined educational elements with entertainment, making space mission planning and managing more approachable and accessible to everyone. In addition, we highly recommend players to see the whole story. Please read the story.
details: Our project is a game meant to make space mission planning and managing accessible for everyone. Compared to regular spacecraft sim engines, this holds several benefits such presenting spacecraft management in a fun and simple way. Although its information about spacecraft managing may be surface-level, it acts as a bridge for newcomers to gain interests about this topic. We vibe coded 90% of our game using ChatGPT Codex, and Claude Code, while also fixing the program separately using VSCode. We mostly used Java Script, along with CSS and HTML to make it accessible through web. Our project is creative because we created the game idea, storyline, gameplay, game mechanics, assets, and music (entirely made by us). In addition, rather than simply teaching players about spacecraft engineering, our game allows the players to experience the challenges of space exploration firsthand through interactive gameplay. While developing this game, our team considered several factors to balance engaging gameplay with educational value. We wanted to make the game entertaining, but not away from the main purpose of the challenge.
